headline: Profit climbs as financing revenue outpaces credit costs
summary_short: Q2 net revenue rose 9.8% y/y to $2,286M and net income climbed 16.5% y/y to $410M, as diluted EPS reached $1.18 versus $1.04 a year ago.
summary_long: Net income rose to $410M (diluted EPS $1.18) on higher net financing revenue — up $168M on larger average earning assets and lower deposit funding costs — plus stronger other revenue, partially offset by a $46M rise in provision for credit losses tied to consumer-auto portfolio growth and $57M higher noninterest expense. Automotive Finance segment pretax income fell to $410M from $472M on higher interest expense and provision; Insurance and Corporate Finance both grew. Net interest margin expanded to 3.59% from 3.41% y/y, CET1 held at 10.15%, and total deposits reached $154.0B. Ally repurchased $148M of common stock and paid a $0.30/share dividend; cash fell to $7.84B on loan growth and preferred-stock refinancing activity.

drivers.explanation: Increase was primarily driven by higher net financing revenue and other interest income and higher total other revenue, partially offset by higher noninterest expense and higher provision expense.
Net financing revenue rose $168M on higher average earning assets and lower interest expense from lower benchmark rates; insurance premiums grew on higher GAP and other F&I volume.
Provision for credit losses rose $46M on consumer-automotive portfolio growth, partially offset by lower net charge-offs; noninterest expense rose $57M on higher compensation and operating expenses.
EPS growth slightly outpaced net income growth after the 0.4% y/y reduction in weighted-average diluted shares from buybacks.
